title: Catégorie des types de mots [dont arbres plans] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous page: a 'graphe circulaire' Γ is a combinatorial map, with oriented edges (darts) A⃗(Γ), a fixed-point-free edge involution σ_Γ and a vertex rotation ρ_Γ. Its face permutation is a single cycle, so it is a one-face (unicellular) map. Its 'contour' C is the face boundary walk: a cyclic polygon whose edge set A(C) is identified with the darts. The polygon carries its fundamental rotation ρ_C = ρ_Γσ_Γ and the involution σ_C = σ_Γ. Conversely ρ_Γ = ρ_C σ_C. So one-face maps are equivalent to polygons equipped with a fixed-point-free involution on their edges.

Top of this page: a boxed summary of the special case.
- 'Arbres plans', unrooted ('non ponctués') and in a plane not necessarily oriented, correspond (≃) to combinatorial polygons with a fixed-point-free involution on the edges that is non-crossing.
- This is the boxed criterion of the previous page: Γ is a tree iff σ_C is a non-crossing perfect matching of the 2n edges of the polygon (genus 0). It is the classical Catalan bijection between plane trees and non-crossing matchings.

Then the general case (any one-face map), topologically:
- The geometric graph |Γ| is the quotient of the circle |C|, subdivided into 2n arcs, by gluing each arc a to the arc σ_C a with reversed orientation.
- This is just the statement that the boundary walk traverses every edge once in each direction.

Tree case, a dual picture:
- View C as the boundary of an oriented disc D subdivided into arcs.
- Join the midpoints of arcs paired by σ_C by pairwise non-intersecting chords (the figure shows such a disc with non-crossing arcs).
- The vertices of Γ correspond to the regions cut out of D: n chords give n+1 regions, which equals the number of vertices of a tree with n edges.
- The oriented edges of Γ correspond to the oriented common frontiers, i.e. the chords with a side.

This is the standard planar-dual description of a plane tree via a non-crossing chord diagram. The page ends mid-sentence; the following sheet in the folder is an unrelated computer printout. Within the folder ('types de mots'), the purpose is presumably to encode plane trees by words, i.e. Dyck-type cyclic words, via the contour.
errors: No mathematical error. The previous page's transcription 'σ_Γ ↔ ρ_C' is almost certainly a misreading: consistency with the other two lines (ρ_Γσ_Γ ↔ ρ_C, ρ_Γ ↔ ρ_C σ_C) requires σ_Γ ↔ σ_C.

Gluing arcs of the circle produces only the 1-dimensional graph |Γ|. To recover the surface of the map one glues the sides of the disc D; the page states only the graph-level quotient, which is correct as stated.

ideas.what: One-face maps encoded as a polygon (boundary walk) with a fixed-point-free involution on its edges; ρ_Γ = ρ_C σ_C
ideas.modern_name: unicellular maps / polygon gluings (permutation encoding of maps)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical: Edmonds, Tutte, Jacques, Cori (1960s–70s); Walsh–Lehman 1972; Harer–Zagier 1986
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) treats maps via permutations and triangulations; the specific contour formulation is unsure

ideas.what: Plane trees ≃ polygons with non-crossing perfect matching of edges
ideas.modern_name: Catalan bijection plane trees ↔ non-crossing matchings (genus-0 unicellular maps)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical combinatorics (Catalan objects; Kreweras 1972 for non-crossing partitions)

ideas.what: |Γ| as the quotient of the subdivided circle gluing a with σa, orientation reversed
ideas.modern_name: contour (boundary-walk) quotient / tree as quotient of a circle (cf. Aldous contour process, gluing of non-crossing matching)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; in probabilistic form Aldous (1991), Le Gall

ideas.what: Dual description: non-crossing chords in a disc; regions are vertices, chords are edges
ideas.modern_name: planar duality between non-crossing chord diagrams and plane trees

deep.surprise_reason: Clean, correct exposition of classical facts (unicellular maps via the contour, plane trees ↔ non-crossing matchings, the tree as a quotient of the circle) in Grothendieck's permutation language of the dessins period. There is nothing beyond the standard literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 4 likely reads 'polygones combinatoires, avec involution sans pts fixes non croisée sur l'ens des arêtes'. The crossed-out word after 'avec' is illegible, and 'non croisée' is underlined/added.
'Revenons au cas d'un graphe Γ circulaire général' is correct; 'quotient par la relation d'équivalence suivante' replaces a crossed-out 'identification'.
On the previous page, the correspondence 'σ_Γ ↔ ρ_C' should almost certainly read σ_Γ ↔ σ_C.
